name: In Memory of the Fallen (undercard)

date.source: The Georgia region's own broadcast dateline.

matches.stipulation: Tournament final for the vacant CWC Georgia State Tag Team Championship
matches.how: John Weyrauch pinned after Ian Walker sprayed mace in his eyes at ringside and Jason Wallace hit a powerbomb.
matches.note: Ian Walker's own interference, blamed on the Supreme Fighting Empire stable, decided the match.

matches.how: Aaron D'Arby retained with a face-first powerbomb, "The Lullaby," after a moonsault body press.

matches.stipulation: CWC Southern States Tag Team Championship
matches.how: Both teams brawled to the outside and were counted out; the ring announcer's own words ruled it a draw, and the Hot House retained.

matches.stipulation: Fifteen-man, over-the-top-rope battle royal for a future CWC Atlanta City Championship match

eliminations.note: Farr kept hold of Martel's own wrist as he went over, pulling Martel off balance.
Farr, already eliminated, added his own weight from the outside; the group pulled Martel over with Jim White caught up in the same tumble.
Caught in the same pile as Martel's own elimination, but credited separately to James.

matches.note: B-Onez won without ever being eliminated, earning a future Atlanta City Championship match against Aaron D'Arby.

matches.how: Jimmy Floyd pinned Logan Gunz with a top-rope frog splash, "Mob Hit," after both men crashed through the timekeeper's table.
Byron Brady forced Aguayfuero to submit to "The Cold Snap," a modified STF crossface, after the match spilled through the crowd and onto the arena roof.

appearances.note: Sprayed mace in John Weyrauch's eyes at ringside to help the Supreme Fighting Empire win the tag title match.
Attacked the injured Southern States Champion after the scaffold match main event, revealing himself as a Supreme Fighting Empire member.
Cornered by Aguayfuero and Johnny Blaze; the reigning Southern States Champion, whose own title defense closed the card.
appearances.source: the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/grw/archive/grw-in-memory-of-the-fallen-1998-05-31.html

appearances.note: Cornered Aguayfuero for his submission match, then Angel Reaper for the scaffold match main event.
The Georgia region's own official, credited with placing the Southern States title match on the scaffold.
appearances.source: the broadcast's own credits, served at /promotions/grw/archive/grw-in-memory-of-the-fallen-1998-05-31.html

notes: The Georgia region's own seven-match supercard of 31 May 1998; six of its seven matches, structured here. The seventh, the scaffold match main event for the CWC Southern States Championship between Angel Reaper and Ian Walker, is already recorded as the Georgia region's own held show and is cross-referenced rather than duplicated. The full document, including that main event, is already served under the Georgia region's own archive.

name: MAPW: Battle Royal for the Vacant Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Championship

notes: The Mid-Atlantic region's own weekly showcase broadcast, culminating in the vacant Heavyweight Championship battle royal; later recapped as archival footage on the region's own 10 February broadcast.

name: MAPW, 8 February 1998

matches.how: Ruled a disqualification after Commander Troyer struck Utah with an American flag pole once the referee, bumped earlier in the match, recovered to see it.
matches.note: A rematch between two of the earlier battle royal's own participants.

appearances.note: Attacked Johnny Utah with Tony Kabaal after his disqualification loss to Commander Troyer.
Attacked Johnny Utah with Frankie Cash after his disqualification loss to Commander Troyer.

notes: Cash and Krash attacked the loser, Johnny Utah, after the match; Commander Troyer ran them off.

name: CWC Weekly Wrap Up

matches.how: Sunflower God finished the newcomer with a top-rope splash.
matches.note: Recapped footage from a Sunday-night Southern region broadcast.

matches.how: The Lane Brothers were counted out after A.J. Speed ran in and attacked Tommy Lane at ringside.
matches.note: Recapped footage from a Sunday-night Southern region broadcast; the Ottoman Empire won the Southern States Tag Team title shot by default.

matches.how: "Iceman" David Smith forced Rick Beltzer to submit to the "Judo Sleeper" after a one-sided beating focused on the leg.
matches.note: Recapped footage from a Mid-Atlantic region broadcast.

matches.how: Richardson retained after the challenger billed as "The Hangman" turned out to be a masked stand-in, "Grave Robber #1"; Richardson finished him with "Stunt City," a modified neckbreaker.
matches.note: Recapped footage from a Mid-Atlantic region broadcast; the crowd was led to expect a genuine Hangman title challenge.

appearances.note: Interrupted a Carolina Crusher/Justin Hawke match with a run-in attack, cut short by the recap's own editing.

Gave a joint interview with tag partner FREEK.

notes: A studio recap broadcast, anchored by Michael Taylor and Jamie West, reviewing the prior week's Southern and Mid-Atlantic region cards and previewing an upcoming pay-per-view with the Georgia region; also carried the returning "Roadkill" Len Griffin's own attack on Tennessee Champion Carolina Crusher, recapped as its own segment.
